Python for LeetCode, but you play it. Every card below is a tiny runnable lesson: the code is real, the output is real. Open the notebook in Jupyter to edit and re-run anything, or just read it as a three-column cheat sheet.

  • ⭐ must-know cards are the ones that show up in a large share of problems.
  • ☆ got it on a card banks 10 XP (saved in your browser) and levels you up.
  • ▶ Visualizers animate the actual function above them line by line, change the input and re-run to see yours.
  • 🧠 Quizzes award XP once per question, and ⚔️ Quests (Jupyter only) are auto-graded boss fights.

Targets Python 3.11 (what LeetCode runs). Anything newer is tagged, e.g. (3.12+).

Enable JavaScript to see your player card.
🔧 Engine 1/3: styles + helpers (the page you’re reading is generated by this notebook) 
import contextlib, copy, html as _html, inspect, io, itertools, json as _json, operator, random, re, signal, sys
from collections import Counter, defaultdict, deque
from IPython.display import HTML, display

_uid = itertools.count(1)

def _esc(x):
    return _html.escape(str(x), quote=True)

def _js(o):
    """JSON that is safe to embed inside a <script> tag."""
    return (_json.dumps(o, separators=(',', ':'))
            .replace('<', '\\u003c').replace('>', '\\u003e').replace('&', '\\u0026'))

_KW = (r'\b(?:def|return|while|for|in|if|elif|else|not|and|or|is|None|True|False|break|continue|'
       r'import|from|yield|lambda|class|pass|nonlocal|global|with|as|try|except|raise)\b')
_TOK = re.compile(r'(#.*$)|("[^"\n]*"|\'[^\'\n]*\')|(' + _KW + r')|(\b\d+(?:\.\d+)?\b)')

def hl(line):
    """Tiny Python syntax highlighter -> HTML."""
    out, pos = [], 0
    for m in _TOK.finditer(line):
        out.append(_esc(line[pos:m.start()]))
        cls = 't-c' if m.group(1) else 't-s' if m.group(2) else 't-k' if m.group(3) else 't-n'
        out.append(f'<span class="{cls}">{_esc(m.group(0))}</span>')
        pos = m.end()
    out.append(_esc(line[pos:]))
    return ''.join(out)

🔧 Engine 2/3: tracer, SVG helpers and the animation player 
# ---------- run a real function and record (line, locals-after-the-line) snapshots ----------
def trace(fn, *args, watch=None, limit=400, drive=None):
    """Run fn(*args) under sys.settrace.
    Returns (events, result) where events = [(line_no_in_source, locals_after_that_line_ran), ...].
    `watch` is a list of substrings; only source lines containing one of them are recorded.
    `drive`, if given, is called instead of fn(*args) (handy to trace several calls of fn)."""
    code = fn.__code__
    first = code.co_firstlineno
    src = inspect.getsource(fn).splitlines()
    keep = None if watch is None else {i + 1 for i, l in enumerate(src) if any(w in l for w in watch)}
    events, st = [], {'pend': None}

    def flush(frame):
        p = st['pend']
        if p is not None and (keep is None or p in keep) and len(events) < limit:
            events.append((p, copy.deepcopy(dict(frame.f_locals))))

    def local(frame, event, arg):
        if event == 'line':
            flush(frame)
            st['pend'] = frame.f_lineno - first + 1
        elif event == 'return':
            flush(frame)
            st['pend'] = None
        return local

    def glob(frame, event, arg):
        if frame.f_code is code:
            st['pend'] = None
            return local
        return None

    old = sys.gettrace()
    sys.settrace(glob)
    try:
        result = drive() if drive else fn(*copy.deepcopy(args))
    finally:
        sys.settrace(old)
    return events, result

def make_frames(fn, args, watch, draw, init, drive=None):
    """Trace fn and turn every recorded snapshot into an animation frame via draw(L, line_text, line_no)."""
    ev, res = trace(fn, *args, watch=watch, drive=drive)
    src = code_of(fn).splitlines()
    frames = [frame(*init)]
    for ln, L in ev:
        frames.append(frame(*draw(L, src[ln - 1].strip(), ln), line=ln))
    return frames, res

def code_of(fn):
    return inspect.getsource(fn).rstrip()

def frame(svg, note='', vars='', line=None):
    return {'svg': svg, 'note': note, 'vars': vars, 'line': line}

def fmt_vars(L, names):
    return ' &nbsp; '.join(f'{n}={_esc(repr(L[n]))}' for n in names if n in L)

# ---------- SVG building blocks (colors: a=blue o=orange g=green r=red p=purple k=gray) ----------
def svg_open(W, H):
    return f'<svg viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" style="max-width:{int(W * 1.35)}px" role="img">'

def arr_svg(vals, *, ptr=None, col=None, dim=(), top=None, cell=40, idx=True):
    """A row of boxes. ptr: {name: index} drawn as ↑name below; col: {index: color}; top: {index: label above}."""
    n = len(vals)
    ptr, col, top = ptr or {}, col or {}, top or {}
    stacks = {}
    for name, i in ptr.items():
        if i is not None and 0 <= i < n:
            stacks.setdefault(i, []).append(name)
    depth = max((len(v) for v in stacks.values()), default=0)
    y0 = 26
    H = y0 + cell + (16 if idx else 4) + 17 * depth + 8
    out = [svg_open(n * cell + 20, H)]
    for i, v in enumerate(vals):
        x = 10 + i * cell
        d = ' dim' if i in dim else ''
        out.append(f'<g class="{d.strip()}"><rect class="b {col.get(i, "")}" x="{x + 2}" y="{y0}" width="{cell - 4}" height="{cell - 4}" rx="6"/>'
                   f'<text x="{x + cell / 2}" y="{y0 + cell / 2 - 2}">{_esc(v)}</text></g>')
        if idx:
            out.append(f'<text class="idx" x="{x + cell / 2}" y="{y0 + cell + 6}">{i}</text>')
        for k, name in enumerate(stacks.get(i, [])):
            out.append(f'<text class="lbl" x="{x + cell / 2}" y="{y0 + cell + (22 if idx else 12) + k * 17}">↑{_esc(name)}</text>')
        if i in top:
            out.append(f'<text class="lbl" x="{x + cell / 2}" y="{y0 - 13}">{_esc(top[i])}</text>')
    out.append('</svg>')
    return ''.join(out)

def graph_svg(pos, edges, *, ncol=None, ecol=None, label=None, badge=None, W=520, H=250, r=18, extra=''):
    ncol, ecol, label, badge = ncol or {}, ecol or {}, label or {}, badge or {}
    out = [svg_open(W, H)]
    for u, v in edges:
        (x1, y1), (x2, y2) = pos[u], pos[v]
        c = ecol.get((u, v)) or ecol.get((v, u)) or ''
        out.append(f'<line class="e {c}" x1="{x1}" y1="{y1}" x2="{x2}" y2="{y2}"/>')
    for n, (x, y) in pos.items():
        out.append(f'<circle class="b {ncol.get(n, "")}" cx="{x}" cy="{y}" r="{r}"/>'
                   f'<text x="{x}" y="{y}">{_esc(label.get(n, n))}</text>')
        if n in badge:
            out.append(f'<text class="lbl" x="{x + r}" y="{y - r}">{badge[n]}</text>')
    out.append(extra + '</svg>')
    return ''.join(out)

def boxes_svg(items, title, *, col=None, W=520, cell=38, hi=None):
    """A labelled strip of boxes, used for queues / stacks."""
    col = col or {}
    n = max(len(items), 1)
    x0 = 14 + int(len(title) * 6.6)
    W = max(W, x0 + (n + 1) * cell + 10)
    out = [svg_open(W, cell + 14), f'<text class="sm l" x="4" y="{cell / 2 + 6}">{_esc(title)}</text>']
    for i, v in enumerate(items):
        x = x0 + i * cell
        out.append(f'<rect class="b {col.get(i, "")}" x="{x}" y="7" width="{cell - 4}" height="{cell - 4}" rx="6"/>'
                   f'<text x="{x + cell / 2 - 2}" y="{cell / 2 + 5}">{_esc(v)}</text>')
    if not items:
        out.append(f'<text class="sm l" x="{x0 + 2}" y="{cell / 2 + 6}" opacity=".5">(empty)</text>')
    out.append('</svg>')
    return ''.join(out)

STEPPER_JS = r"""
(function(){
var root=document.getElementById('__ID__');
if(!root||root.getAttribute('data-ready'))return;
root.setAttribute('data-ready','1');
var D=JSON.parse(root.querySelector('script[type="application/json"]').textContent);
var names=Object.keys(D.v),cur=names[0],i=0,timer=null,ms=900;
function q(s){return root.querySelector(s)}
var stage=q('.lc-stage'),note=q('.lc-note'),vars=q('.lc-vars'),code=q('.lc-code'),
    rng=q('.lc-rng'),pos=q('.lc-pos'),play=q('.lc-play'),spd=q('.lc-spd');
function F(){return D.v[cur].frames}
function show(){
  var fr=F()[i];
  stage.innerHTML=fr.svg;note.innerHTML=fr.note||'';vars.innerHTML=fr.vars||'';
  var ls=code.querySelectorAll('.ln');
  for(var k=0;k<ls.length;k++){ls[k].classList.toggle('on',k+1===fr.line)}
  rng.max=F().length-1;rng.value=i;pos.textContent=(i+1)+' / '+F().length;
  if(i===F().length-1){stop();
    if(D.xp)window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('lc-earn',{detail:{id:D.xp,xp:5}}))}
}
function build(){
  var c=D.v[cur].code;
  code.innerHTML=c?c.map(function(l){return '<span class="ln">'+l+'</span>'}).join(''):'';
  code.style.display=c?'':'none';
  var ts=root.querySelectorAll('.lc-tab');
  for(var k=0;k<ts.length;k++)ts[k].classList.toggle('on',ts[k].getAttribute('data-v')===cur);
}
function go(n){i=Math.max(0,Math.min(F().length-1,n));show()}
function stop(){if(timer){clearInterval(timer);timer=null}play.textContent='▶'}
function start(){
  if(i>=F().length-1)go(0);
  play.textContent='⏸';
  timer=setInterval(function(){if(i>=F().length-1){stop();return}go(i+1)},ms);
}
q('.lc-first').onclick=function(){stop();go(0)};
q('.lc-prev').onclick=function(){stop();go(i-1)};
q('.lc-next').onclick=function(){stop();go(i+1)};
q('.lc-last').onclick=function(){stop();go(1e9)};
play.onclick=function(){timer?stop():start()};
rng.oninput=function(){stop();go(+rng.value)};
spd.onchange=function(){ms=+spd.value;if(timer){stop();start()}};
Array.prototype.forEach.call(root.querySelectorAll('.lc-tab'),function(b){
  b.onclick=function(){stop();cur=b.getAttribute('data-v');i=0;build();show()}});
root.addEventListener('keydown',function(e){
  if(e.key==='ArrowRight'){stop();go(i+1);e.preventDefault()}
  else if(e.key==='ArrowLeft'){stop();go(i-1);e.preventDefault()}
  else if(e.key===' '&&e.target===root){play.click();e.preventDefault()}});
build();show();
})();
"""

def stepper(variants, *, xp_id=None):
    """variants: {tab name: {'frames': [frame(...)...], 'code': source or None}}"""
    uid = f'lcs{next(_uid)}'
    data = {'xp': xp_id, 'v': {
        name: {'frames': v['frames'], 'code': [hl(l) for l in v['code'].splitlines()] if v.get('code') else None}
        for name, v in variants.items()}}
    tabs = ''
    if len(variants) > 1:
        tabs = '<div class="lc-tabs">' + ''.join(
            f'<button type="button" class="lc-tab" data-v="{_esc(n)}">{_esc(n)}</button>' for n in variants) + '</div>'
    xp = f' data-lc-ids="{_esc(xp_id)}" data-lc-each="5"' if xp_id else ''
    display(HTML(
        f'<div class="lc-w lc-stp" id="{uid}" tabindex="0"{xp}>{tabs}'
        '<div class="lc-body"><pre class="lc-code"></pre><div class="lc-sw"><div class="lc-stage"></div>'
        '<div class="lc-note"></div><div class="lc-vars"></div></div></div>'
        '<div class="lc-ctl"><button type="button" class="lc-first" aria-label="first">⏮</button>'
        '<button type="button" class="lc-prev" aria-label="previous">◀</button>'
        '<button type="button" class="lc-play" aria-label="play or pause">▶</button>'
        '<button type="button" class="lc-next" aria-label="next">▶|</button>'
        '<button type="button" class="lc-last" aria-label="last">⏭</button>'
        '<input class="lc-rng" type="range" min="0" max="0" value="0" aria-label="step">'
        '<select class="lc-spd" aria-label="speed"><option value="1500">0.5×</option><option value="900" selected>1×</option>'
        '<option value="450">2×</option><option value="200">4×</option></select><span class="lc-pos"></span></div>'
        f'<script type="application/json">{_js(data)}</script>'
        f'<script>{STEPPER_JS.replace("__ID__", uid)}</script></div>'))
🔧 Engine 3/3: quiz player, Big-O calculator, quest grader 
QUIZ_JS = r"""
(function(){
var root=document.getElementById('__ID__');
if(!root||root.getAttribute('data-ready'))return;
root.setAttribute('data-ready','1');
var D=JSON.parse(root.querySelector('script[type="application/json"]').textContent);
var n=0,score=0,answered=false,body=root.querySelector('.lc-qbody');
function render(){
  if(n>=D.qs.length){done();return}
  var Q=D.qs[n];answered=false;
  var h='<div class="lc-qhead">'+D.title+' · '+(n+1)+' / '+D.qs.length+'</div><div class="q">'+Q.q+'</div>';
  Q.c.forEach(function(c,k){h+='<button type="button" class="ch" data-k="'+k+'">'+c+'</button>'});
  h+='<div class="why" style="display:none"></div><button type="button" class="nx" style="display:none">'+(n+1<D.qs.length?'Next →':'Finish')+'</button>';
  body.innerHTML=h;
  var btns=body.querySelectorAll('.ch');
  Array.prototype.forEach.call(btns,function(b){b.onclick=function(){
    if(answered)return;answered=true;
    var k=+b.getAttribute('data-k'),ok=k===Q.a;
    if(ok){score++;window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('lc-earn',{detail:{id:Q.id,xp:D.xp}}))}
    btns[Q.a].classList.add('ok');if(!ok)b.classList.add('no');
    var w=body.querySelector('.why');w.style.display='';w.innerHTML=(ok?'✅ ':'❌ ')+Q.why;
    body.querySelector('.nx').style.display='';
  }});
  body.querySelector('.nx').onclick=function(){n++;render()};
}
function done(){
  body.innerHTML='<div class="lc-qhead">'+D.title+'</div><div class="q">Score: '+score+' / '+D.qs.length+(score===D.qs.length?' 🏆':'')+'</div><button type="button" class="nx">↻ Play again</button>';
  body.querySelector('.nx').onclick=function(){n=0;score=0;render()};
}
render();
})();
"""

def quiz(title, qs, *, key, xp=5):
    """qs: [{'id','q','choices':[html...],'a':index,'why':html}]"""
    uid = f'lcq{next(_uid)}'
    data = {'title': _esc(title), 'xp': xp,
            'qs': [{'id': f'{key}:{q["id"]}', 'q': q['q'], 'c': q['choices'], 'a': q['a'], 'why': q['why']} for q in qs]}
    ids = ','.join(q['id'] for q in data['qs'])
    display(HTML(
        f'<div class="lc-w lc-quiz" id="{uid}" data-lc-ids="{_esc(ids)}" data-lc-each="{xp}"><div class="lc-qbody"></div>'
        f'<script type="application/json">{_js(data)}</script><script>{QUIZ_JS.replace("__ID__", uid)}</script></div>'))

def _code(s):
    return f'<code>{_esc(s)}</code>'

def trap(id, code, wrong, why):
    """'What does this print?' question: the right answer is computed by really running the snippet."""
    buf = io.StringIO()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf):
        exec(code, {})
    right = buf.getvalue().strip()
    assert right not in wrong, (right, wrong)
    choices = [right] + list(wrong)
    random.Random(id).shuffle(choices)
    return {'id': id, 'q': f'What does this print?<pre>{_esc(code.strip())}</pre>',
            'choices': [_code(c) for c in choices], 'a': choices.index(right),
            'why': f'It prints {_code(right)}. {why}'}

def pick(id, q, choices, answer, why):
    choices = list(choices)
    return {'id': id, 'q': q, 'choices': choices, 'a': choices.index(answer), 'why': why}

BIGO_JS = r"""
(function(){
var root=document.getElementById('__ID__');
if(!root||root.getAttribute('data-ready'))return;
root.setAttribute('data-ready','1');
var rows=[['O(1)',function(n){return 0}],['O(log n)',function(n){return Math.log10(Math.max(1,Math.log2(n)))}],
 ['O(n)',function(n){return Math.log10(n)}],['O(n log n)',function(n){return Math.log10(n*Math.max(1,Math.log2(n)))}],
 ['O(n²)',function(n){return 2*Math.log10(n)}],['O(n³)',function(n){return 3*Math.log10(n)}],
 ['O(2ⁿ)',function(n){return n*Math.log10(2)}],
 ['O(n!)',function(n){return n<2?0:(n*Math.log10(n/Math.E)+0.5*Math.log10(2*Math.PI*n))}]];
var BUDGET=7,CAP=12;
var rng=root.querySelector('input'),nl=root.querySelector('.nval'),box=root.querySelector('.rows');
box.innerHTML=rows.map(function(r){return '<div class="row"><b>'+r[0]+'</b><div class="track"><i></i></div><span class="ops"></span></div>'}).join('');
function fmt(l){return l<4?String(Math.round(Math.pow(10,l))):'10^'+l.toFixed(1)}
function upd(){
  var n=Math.max(1,Math.round(Math.pow(10,+rng.value)));
  nl.textContent='n = '+n.toLocaleString();
  var els=box.querySelectorAll('.row');
  rows.forEach(function(r,k){
    var l=Math.max(0,r[1](n)),bar=els[k].querySelector('i'),op=els[k].querySelector('.ops');
    bar.style.width=Math.min(100,100*l/CAP)+'%';
    bar.style.background=l<=BUDGET?'#22c55e':(l<=BUDGET+1?'#f59e0b':'#ef4444');
    op.textContent='≈ '+(l>300?'∞':fmt(l))+' ops';

}

def bigo_widget():
    uid = f'lcb{next(_uid)}'
    display(HTML(
        f'<div class="lc-w lc-bigo" id="{uid}"><div class="lc-qhead">Drag n: green fits a ~10⁷-operation Python budget, '
        'amber is borderline (10⁸), red will time out</div>'
        '<div><b class="nval"></b></div><input type="range" min="0.3" max="9" step="0.05" value="5">'
        f'<div class="rows"></div><script>{BIGO_JS.replace("__ID__", uid)}</script></div>'))

# ---------- quests (auto-graded exercises, Jupyter only) ----------
_SAVE = {'coins': 0, 'cleared': {}}
_TOTAL_QUESTS = 7

class _Timeout(Exception):
    pass

@contextlib.contextmanager
def _limit(sec):
    armed = False
    try:
        def _h(*_):
            raise _Timeout()
        old = signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, _h)
        signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, sec)
        armed = True
    except Exception:
        pass
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        if armed:
            signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, 0)
            signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, old)

def _short(x, n=70):
    s = repr(x)
    return s if len(s) <= n else s[:n - 1] + '…'

def run_quest(q, fn):
    rows, passed, untouched = [], 0, True
    for args, want, *cmp in q['tests']:
        same = cmp[0] if cmp else operator.eq
        err = None
        try:
            with _limit(2):
                got = fn(*copy.deepcopy(args))
        except _Timeout:
            got, err = None, 'timed out (> 2 s)'
        except BaseException as e:
            got, err = None, f'{type(e).__name__}: {e}'
        try:
            ok = err is None and bool(same(got, want))
        except Exception:
            ok = False
        if err or got is not None:
            untouched = False
        passed += ok
        rows.append((ok, args, want, err or got))
    return rows, passed, untouched

def play(key, fn):
    q = QUESTS[key]
    rows, passed, untouched = run_quest(q, fn)
    total = len(rows)
    first_clear = passed == total and key not in _SAVE['cleared']
    if first_clear:
        _SAVE['cleared'][key] = q['coins']
        _SAVE['coins'] += q['coins']
    if passed == total:
        status = f'✅ <b>Quest cleared!</b> ' + (f'+{q["coins"]} 🪙' if first_clear else '(reward already claimed)')
    elif untouched:
        status = f'🎯 <b>Quest open.</b> Edit the function above and re-run this cell. {total} hidden tests are waiting.'
    else:
        status = f'🛠️ <b>{passed} / {total} tests pass.</b> Keep going.'
    shown = rows if passed == total else [r for r in rows if not r[0]][:4]
    body = ''.join(
        f'<tr><td>{"✔" if ok else "✘"}</td><td>{_esc(_short(a if len(a) > 1 else a[0]))}</td><td>{_esc(_short(w))}</td><td>{_esc(_short(g))}</td></tr>'
        for ok, a, w, g in shown) if not untouched else ''
    table = ('<table><tr><th></th><th>input</th><th>expected</th><th>got</th></tr>' + body + '</table>') if body else ''
    hint = f'<details><summary>💡 hint</summary>{q["hint"]}</details>' if q.get('hint') else ''
    cls = 'cleared' if passed == total else ''
    display(HTML(f'<div class="lc-w lc-quest {cls}"><div class="lc-qt">⚔️ <b>{_esc(q["title"])}</b> &nbsp;·&nbsp; 🪙 {q["coins"]}</div>'
                 f'<div class="lc-qs">{status}</div>{table}{hint}</div>'))

def scoreboard():
    names = {k: v['title'] for k, v in QUESTS.items()}
    n = len(_SAVE['cleared'])
    rank = ['Rookie', 'Apprentice', 'Apprentice', 'Adventurer', 'Adventurer', 'Veteran', 'Veteran', 'Legend'][min(n, 7)]
    chips = ''.join(f'<span class="{"" if k in _SAVE["cleared"] else "off"}">{"✔ " if k in _SAVE["cleared"] else ""}{_esc(t)}</span>'
                    for k, t in names.items())
    display(HTML(f'<div class="lc-w lc-score"><div class="big">🪙 {_SAVE["coins"]} coins &nbsp;·&nbsp; {n} / {_TOTAL_QUESTS} quests &nbsp;·&nbsp; {rank}</div>'
                 f'<div class="chips">{chips}</div></div>'))

The Solution skeleton

LeetCode gives you a class (and pre-imports List, Optional, …). Locally, just call it yourself.

class Solution:
    def twoSum(self, nums, target):
        seen = {}                  # value -> index
        for i, x in enumerate(nums):
            if target - x in seen:
                return [seen[target - x], i]
            seen[x] = i

print(Solution().twoSum([2, 7, 11, 15], 9))
[0, 1]

Constraints → complexity

Python does roughly 10⁷ simple operations per second, so budget ~10× tighter than C++. Read n in the problem, then pick the algorithm.

n ≤ aim for
10 O(n!)
20 O(2ⁿ)
500 O(n³)
5 000 O(n²)
10⁵ O(n log n)
10⁶ O(n)
10⁹+ O(log n), O(1)

Cost of common operations

op cost
list.append / pop() O(1)
list.pop(0) / insert(0, x) O(n)
x in list O(n)
x in set / dict O(1)
deque.append / popleft O(1)
heappush / heappop O(log n)
heapify O(n)
sorted / list.sort O(n log n)
s[a:b] (slice) O(b − a)
s1 + s2 O(len)
min / max / sum O(n)

Bit tricks

n & (n-1) clears the lowest set bit. n & -n isolates it. XOR cancels pairs.

Palindromes & anagrams

from collections import Counter

def is_palindrome(s):
    t = [c.lower() for c in s if c.isalnum()]
    return t == t[::-1]

print(is_palindrome('A man, a plan, a canal: Panama'))
print(sorted('listen') == sorted('silent'), Counter('abc') == Counter('cab'))
print(''.join(sorted('eat')), tuple(sorted(Counter('eat').items())))   # grouping keys

def longest_pal(s):                          # expand around centre
    best = ''
    for c in range(len(s)):
        for l, r in ((c, c), (c, c + 1)):
            while l >= 0 and r < len(s) and s[l] == s[r]:
                l, r = l - 1, r + 1
            best = max(best, s[l + 1:r], key=len)
    return best

print(longest_pal('babad'))

Never build a grid with [[0] * m] * n: every row is the same list.

2D grid idioms

DIRS + a bounds check is the backbone of every grid problem.

from itertools import product

g = [[1, 2, 3],
     [4, 5, 6]]
R, C = len(g), len(g[0])
DIRS = ((1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1))

def neighbors(r, c):
    for dr, dc in DIRS:
        nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
        if 0 <= nr < R and 0 <= nc < C:
            yield nr, nc

print(list(neighbors(0, 0)), len(list(neighbors(1, 1))))
print(list(zip(*g)))                           # transpose
print([list(r) for r in zip(*g[::-1])])        # rotate 90° clockwise
print([x for row in g for x in row], sum(map(sum, g)))
print([row[:] for row in g] == g, list(product(range(2), range(2))))
[(1, 0), (0, 1)] 3
[(1, 4), (2, 5), (3, 6)]
[[4, 1], [5, 2], [6, 3]]
[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6] 21
True [(0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0), (1, 1)]

Prefix sums

P[i] = sum of the first i items, so sum(a[l:r]) == P[r] - P[l] in O(1).

from itertools import accumulate

a = [3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9]
P = [0] + list(accumulate(a))
print(P, P[5] - P[2])                          # sum(a[2:5])
print(list(accumulate(a, max)))                # running max

[3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 9]

Hashing patterns

Complement lookup, first-seen index, and tuple(...) to use a list as a key.

def two_sum(nums, target):
    pos = {}
    for i, x in enumerate(nums):
        if target - x in pos:
            return pos[target - x], i
        pos[x] = i

OrderedDict & LRU cache

Plain dicts already keep insertion order. OrderedDict adds move_to_end and popitem(last=False).

from collections import OrderedDict

class LRU:
    def __init__(self, cap):
        self.cap, self.d = cap, OrderedDict()
    def get(self, k):
        if k not in self.d:
            return -1
        self.d.move_to_end(k)
        return self.d[k]
    def put(self, k, v):
        self.d[k] = v
        self.d.move_to_end(k)
        if len(self.d) > self.cap:
            self.d.popitem(last=False)

c = LRU(2)
c.put('a', 1); c.put('b', 2); c.get('a'); c.put('c', 3)
print(list(c.d), c.get('b'))
['a', 'c'] -1

World 6 · Stacks & Queues

Stack = list

append pushes, pop() pops, st[-1] peeks. Always guard with if st:.

def is_valid(s):
    pair = {')': '(', ']': '[', '}': '{'}
    st = []
    for ch in s:
        if ch in pair:
            if not st or st.pop() != pair[ch]:
                return False
        else:
            st.append(ch)
    return not st

print(is_valid('{[()]}'), is_valid('(]'), is_valid('(('))
True False False

Monotonic stack

Keep a stack whose values only go one direction. Each element is pushed and popped once: O(n) for “next greater / smaller” questions.

def next_greater(a):
    res = [-1] * len(a)
    st = []                            # indices, values decreasing
    for i, x in enumerate(a):
        while st and a[st[-1]] < x:
            res[st.pop()] = x
        st.append(i)
    return res

print(next_greater([2, 1, 2, 4, 3]))
[4, 2, 4, -1, -1]

Binary search template


Pick one invariant and stick to it. This one searches the closed range [lo, hi].




def binary_search(a, target):
    lo, hi = 0, len(a) - 1
    while lo <= hi:
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        if a[mid] == target:
            return mid
        if a[mid] < target:
            lo = mid + 1
        else:
            hi = mid - 1
    return -1

print(binary_search([1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11], 7), binary_search([1, 3, 5], 4))

Binary search on the answer


If “can I do it with speed k?” flips from No to Yes exactly once, binary search k. (LC 875, 1011, 410 …)




def min_eating_speed(piles, h):
    lo, hi = 1, max(piles)                      # smallest k that works
    while lo < hi:
        k = (lo + hi) // 2
        hours = sum(-(-p // k) for p in piles)  # ceil(p / k)
        if hours <= h:
            hi = k                              # k works: try smaller
        else:
            lo = k + 1
    return lo

Intervals


Sort by start, then sweep. Two intervals overlap iff a_start < b_end and b_start < a_end.




def merge(intervals):
    out = []
    for s, e in sorted(intervals):
        if out and s <= out[-1][1]:
            out[-1][1] = max(out[-1][1], e)
        else:
            out.append([s, e])
    return out

Top-k with a size-k heap


Keep a min-heap of the k largest seen. Its root is the k-th largest. O(n log k).




def kth_largest(nums, k):
    h = []
    for x in nums:
        heappush(h, x)
        if len(h) > k:
            heappop(h)
    return h[0]

Heap internals


What heappush / heappop do (a textbook version; CPython’s C code sifts a little differently but is equivalent).




def heap_push(h, x):
    h.append(x)
    i = len(h) - 1
    while i > 0:
        p = (i - 1) // 2
        if h[p] <= h[i]:
            break
        h[p], h[i] = h[i], h[p]
        i = p

def heap_pop(h):
    top, last = h[0], h.pop()
    if h:
        h[0] = last
        i = 0
        while True:
            l, r, m = 2 * i + 1, 2 * i + 2, i
            if l < len(h) and h[l] < h[m]:
                m = l
            if r < len(h) and h[r] < h[m]:
                m = r
            if m == i:
                break
            h[i], h[m] = h[m], h[i]
            i = m
    return top

h = []
for x in [5, 3, 8, 1, 9, 2]:
    heap_push(h, x)
print(h)                                # parent of i is (i-1)//2, children 2i+1 and 2i+2
print([heap_pop(h) for _ in range(len(h))])

🔧 how this animation is built

def heap_svg(h, col=None):
    col = col or {}
    W, n = 520, len(h)
    levels = max(1, (n).bit_length())
    H = 30 + 52 * levels
    pos = {}
    for i in range(n):
        lv = (i + 1).bit_length() - 1
        k = i - (2 ** lv - 1)
        pos[i] = (W * (k + .5) / 2 ** lv, 26 + 52 * lv)
    out = [svg_open(W, H)]
    for i in range(1, n):
        (x1, y1), (x2, y2) = pos[(i - 1) // 2], pos[i]
        out.append(f'<line class="e" x1="{x1}" y1="{y1}" x2="{x2}" y2="{y2}"/>')
    for i in range(n):
        x, y = pos[i]
        out.append(f'<circle class="b {col.get(i, "")}" cx="{x}" cy="{y}" r="18"/><text x="{x}" y="{y}">{h[i]}</text>')
    out.append('</svg>')
    return ''.join(out)

def viz_heap(push_fn, pop_fn, values):
    popped = []

    def draw_push(L, txt, ln):
        h, i, p = L['h'], L.get('i'), L.get('p')
        col = {}
        if 'append' in txt:
            col[len(h) - 1] = 'o'
            note = f'push <b>{L["x"]}</b>: append it at the end (index {len(h) - 1})'
        elif 'break' in txt:
            col = {i: 'g', (i - 1) // 2: 'g'} if i else {}
            note = 'parent ≤ child: heap property holds, stop'
        else:
            col = {p: 'o', i: 'a'}
            note = f'child {h[i]} &lt; parent: swap them, the smaller value moves <b>up</b>'
        return heap_svg(h, col) + arr_svg(h, col=col), note, fmt_vars(L, ['x', 'i', 'p'])

    def draw_pop(L, txt, ln):
        h, i, m = L['h'], L.get('i'), L.get('m')
        col = {}
        if 'return top' in txt:
            popped.append(L['top'])
            note = f'popped the minimum <b>{L["top"]}</b> (so far: {popped})'
        elif 'h[0] = last' in txt:
            col = {0: 'o'}
            note = f'move the last leaf ({L["last"]}) to the root, then sift it <b>down</b>'
        else:
            col = {i: 'a', m: 'o'}
            note = f'swap with the smaller child: it moves <b>up</b>, {h[m]} sinks down'
        return heap_svg(h, col) + arr_svg(h, col=col), note, fmt_vars(L, ['top', 'last', 'i', 'm'])

    hp = []
    pf, _ = make_frames(push_fn, (hp, 0), ['h.append(x)', 'h[p], h[i] = h[i], h[p]', 'break'], draw_push,
                        (heap_svg([]), f'Pushing {values} one by one into an empty heap.', ''),
                        drive=lambda: [push_fn(hp, x) for x in values])
    hp2 = list(hp)
    qf, _ = make_frames(pop_fn, (hp2,), ['h[0] = last', 'h[i], h[m] = h[m], h[i]', 'return top'], draw_pop,
                        (heap_svg(hp2) + arr_svg(hp2), f'Popping 3 times from the heap {hp2}.', ''),
                        drive=lambda: [pop_fn(hp2) for _ in range(3)])
    stepper({'heap_push (sift up)': {'frames': pf, 'code': code_of(push_fn)},
             'heap_pop (sift down)': {'frames': qf, 'code': code_of(pop_fn)}}, xp_id='viz:heap')

functools: cache & reduce


@cache (3.9+) memoizes a pure function: instant top-down DP. Arguments must be hashable, so pass tuples, not lists.




from functools import cache, lru_cache, reduce

@cache
def fib(n):
    return n if n < 2 else fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2)

print(fib(80), fib.cache_info().currsize)
print(reduce(lambda a, b: a * b, [1, 2, 3, 4]), reduce(max, [3, 9, 2]))

@lru_cache(maxsize=None)                         # same thing, works on 3.8
def paths(r, c):
    return 1 if r == 0 or c == 0 else paths(r - 1, c) + paths(r, c - 1)

print(paths(10, 10))

World 10 · Recursion & Backtracking




Recursion toolkit


Define a helper inside the method and capture variables from the enclosing scope. Use nonlocal to rebind them.




import sys
sys.setrecursionlimit(10**5)        # default is ~1000; deep DFS needs more

def count_paths(grid):
    R, C = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    total = 0
    def dfs(r, c):
        nonlocal total
        if r == R - 1 and c == C - 1:
            total += 1
            return
        for nr, nc in ((r + 1, c), (r, c + 1)):
            if nr < R and nc < C and grid[nr][nc] == 0:
                dfs(nr, nc)
    dfs(0, 0)
    return total

print(count_paths([[0, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0], [0, 0, 0]]))




2










Backtracking template


Choose → explore → un-choose. Copy the path (path[:]) when you record it.




def subsets(nums):
    res, path = [], []
    def dfs(i):
        if i == len(nums):
            res.append(path[:])
            return
        dfs(i + 1)                  # skip nums[i]
        path.append(nums[i])        # take it
        dfs(i + 1)
        path.pop()                  # undo
    dfs(0)
    return res

print(subsets([1, 2, 3]))




[[], [3], [2], [2, 3], [1], [1, 3], [1, 2], [1, 2, 3]]










Permutations & combination sum




def permute(nums):
    res, path, used = [], [], [False] * len(nums)
    def dfs():
        if len(path) == len(nums):
            res.append(path[:])
            return
        for i, x in enumerate(nums):
            if not used[i]:
                used[i] = True; path.append(x)
                dfs()
                used[i] = False; path.pop()
    dfs()
    return res

def combination_sum(cands, target):
    res = []
    def dfs(start, path, left):
        if left == 0:
            res.append(path[:])
        for i in range(start, len(cands)):
            if cands[i] <= left:
                path.append(cands[i])
                dfs(i, path, left - cands[i])      # i, not i+1: reuse allowed
                path.pop()
    dfs(0, [], target)
    return res

print(permute([1, 2, 3]))
print(combination_sum([2, 3, 6, 7], 7))

Skip duplicates




def subsets_unique(nums):
    nums.sort()
    res = []
    def dfs(start, path):
        res.append(path[:])
        for i in range(start, len(nums)):
            if i > start and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]:
                continue                      # same value at this depth: skip
            path.append(nums[i])
            dfs(i + 1, path)
            path.pop()
    dfs(0, [])
    return res

print(subsets_unique([1, 2, 2]))

World 11 · Linked Lists & Trees




ListNode & test helpers


LeetCode supplies ListNode. You need from_list / to_list to test locally.




class ListNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, next=None):
        self.val, self.next = val, next

def from_list(vals):
    dummy = cur = ListNode()
    for v in vals:
        cur.next = ListNode(v)
        cur = cur.next
    return dummy.next

def to_list(head):
    out = []
    while head:
        out.append(head.val)
        head = head.next
    return out

print(to_list(from_list([1, 2, 3])))




[1, 2, 3]










Dummy head & merging


A dummy node removes the “is this the first node?” special case.




def merge_two(a, b):
    dummy = tail = ListNode()
    while a and b:
        if a.val <= b.val:
            tail.next, a = a, a.next
        else:
            tail.next, b = b, b.next
        tail = tail.next
    tail.next = a or b
    return dummy.next

Fast & slow pointers




def middle(head):
    slow = fast = head
    while fast and fast.next:
        slow, fast = slow.next, fast.next.next
    return slow

def has_cycle(head):
    slow = fast = head
    while fast and fast.next:
        slow, fast = slow.next, fast.next.next
        if slow is fast:
            return True
    return False

Reverse a list




def reverse_list(head):
    prev, cur = None, head
    while cur:
        nxt = cur.next
        cur.next = prev
        prev, cur = cur, nxt
    return prev

def ll_svg(L, vals):
    W, H, step = 24 + len(vals) * 84, 130, 84
    xs = {v: 12 + i * step for i, v in enumerate(vals)}
    nodes, stack = {}, [L.get(k) for k in ('head', 'prev', 'cur', 'nxt')]
    while stack:
        n = stack.pop()
        if n is not None and n.val not in nodes:
            nodes[n.val] = n
            stack.append(n.next)
    out = [svg_open(W, H), '<defs><marker id="lcah" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto"><path class="ar" d="M0 0L10 5L0 10z"/></marker></defs>']
    for v, n in nodes.items():
        x = xs[v]
        c = 'g' if L.get('cur') is not None and L['cur'].val == v else ''
        out.append(f'<rect class="b {c}" x="{x}" y="34" width="44" height="34" rx="7"/><text x="{x + 22}" y="51">{v}</text>')
        if n.next is None:
            out.append(f'<text class="sm" x="{x + 22}" y="16">∅</text><line class="e" x1="{x + 22}" y1="24" x2="{x + 22}" y2="33"/>')
        else:
            x2 = xs[n.next.val]
            if x2 > x:
                out.append(f'<line class="e" x1="{x + 44}" y1="46" x2="{x2 - 3}" y2="46" marker-end="url(#lcah)"/>')
            else:
                out.append(f'<line class="e a" x1="{x}" y1="58" x2="{x2 + 47}" y2="58" marker-end="url(#lcah)"/>')
    tags = {}
    for k in ('head', 'prev', 'cur', 'nxt'):
        if L.get(k) is not None:
            tags.setdefault(L[k].val, []).append(k)
    for v, ks in tags.items():
        for j, k in enumerate(ks):
            out.append(f'<text class="lbl" x="{xs[v] + 22}" y="{86 + 16 * j}">↑{k}</text>')
    out.append('</svg>')
    return ''.join(out)

def viz_reverse_list(fn, vals):

        who = lambda k: 'None' if L.get(k) is None else L[k].val
        if txt.startswith('prev, cur = None'):
            note = 'prev = None (nothing reversed yet), cur = head'
        elif 'nxt = cur.next' in txt:
            note = f'remember what comes next: nxt = {who("nxt")} (we are about to cut the link)'
        elif 'cur.next = prev' in txt:

        elif 'prev, cur =' in txt:

        else:
            note = f'cur is None: done. prev ({who("prev")}) is the new head'
        return ll_svg(L, vals), note, ' &nbsp; '.join(f'{k}={who(k)}' for k in ('prev', 'cur', 'nxt') if k in L)

    frames, _ = make_frames(fn, (head,), ['prev, cur = None', 'nxt = cur.next', 'cur.next = prev', 'prev, cur = cur, nxt', 'return prev'],
                            draw, (ll_svg({'head': head}, vals), 'Three pointers walk the list and flip one arrow per step.', ''))
    stepper({'reverse_list': {'frames': frames, 'code': code_of(fn)}}, xp_id='viz:reverse_list')

TreeNode & build_tree


LeetCode shows trees as a level-order list with None for gaps. This helper builds one so you can test.




class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val, self.left, self.right = val, left, right

def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] is None:
        return None
    root = TreeNode(vals[0])
    q, i = deque([root]), 1
    while q and i < len(vals):
        node = q.popleft()
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] is not None:
            node.left = TreeNode(vals[i]); q.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] is not None:
            node.right = TreeNode(vals[i]); q.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root

def height(n):
    return 0 if n is None else 1 + max(height(n.left), height(n.right))

DFS traversals


Pre = node first, in = node between (sorted order for a BST), post = node last.




def preorder(n):
    return [n.val] + preorder(n.left) + preorder(n.right) if n else []

def inorder(n):
    return inorder(n.left) + [n.val] + inorder(n.right) if n else []

def postorder(n):
    return postorder(n.left) + postorder(n.right) + [n.val] if n else []

BFS: level order


for _ in range(len(q)) processes exactly one level at a time.




def level_order(root):
    res, q = [], deque([root] if root else [])
    while q:
        level = []
        for _ in range(len(q)):
            n = q.popleft()
            level.append(n.val)
            if n.left:
                q.append(n.left)
            if n.right:
                q.append(n.right)
        res.append(level)
    return res

Iterative inorder & BST checks




def inorder_iter(root):
    res, st, cur = [], [], root
    while cur or st:
        while cur:
            st.append(cur)
            cur = cur.left
        cur = st.pop()
        res.append(cur.val)
        cur = cur.right
    return res

def is_bst(n, lo=-inf, hi=inf):
    return n is None or (lo < n.val < hi and is_bst(n.left, lo, n.val) and is_bst(n.right, n.val, hi))

def lca(n, p, q):                       # lowest common ancestor in a BST
    while n:
        if p < n.val and q < n.val:
            n = n.left
        elif p > n.val and q > n.val:
            n = n.right
        else:
            return n.val

def tree_svg(root, order=(), cur=None):
    pos, ctr = {}, [0]
    def go(n, d):
        if n is None:
            return
        go(n.left, d + 1); pos[n] = (ctr[0], d); ctr[0] += 1; go(n.right, d + 1)
    go(root, 0)
    n_nodes = len(pos)
    depth = max(d for _, d in pos.values()) + 1
    W, H = 40 + n_nodes * 46, 20 + depth * 56
    xy = {n: (30 + i * 46, 24 + d * 56) for n, (i, d) in pos.items()}
    out = [svg_open(W, H)]
    for n, (x, y) in xy.items():
        for ch in (n.left, n.right):
            if ch is not None:
                out.append(f'<line class="e" x1="{x}" y1="{y}" x2="{xy[ch][0]}" y2="{xy[ch][1]}"/>')
    for n, (x, y) in xy.items():
        c = 'o' if n.val == cur else 'a' if n.val in order else ''
        out.append(f'<circle class="b {c}" cx="{x}" cy="{y}" r="17"/><text x="{x}" y="{y}">{n.val}</text>')
        if n.val in order:

BFS & DFS


BFS (queue) finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs. DFS (stack/recursion) explores deep first.




G = {0: [1, 2], 1: [0, 3, 4], 2: [0, 5], 3: [1, 6], 4: [1, 6], 5: [2, 6], 6: [3, 4, 5, 7], 7: [6]}

def bfs(g, start):
    seen = {start}
    q = deque([start])
    order = []
    while q:
        u = q.popleft()
        order.append(u)
        for v in g[u]:
            if v not in seen:
                seen.add(v)
                q.append(v)
    return order

def dfs(g, start):
    seen, order = set(), []
    stack = [start]
    while stack:
        u = stack.pop()
        if u in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(u)
        order.append(u)
        for v in g[u]:
            if v not in seen:
                stack.append(v)
    return order

Grid BFS


Shortest path in a maze / flood fill. Mark cells as seen when you enqueue them, not when you pop.




def shortest_path(grid, start, goal):
    R, C = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    q = deque([(*start, 0)])
    seen = {start}
    while q:
        r, c, d = q.popleft()
        if (r, c) == goal:
            return d
        for dr, dc in ((1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1)):
            nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
            if (0 <= nr < R and 0 <= nc < C
                    and grid[nr][nc] != '#' and (nr, nc) not in seen):
                seen.add((nr, nc))
                q.append((nr, nc, d + 1))
    return -1

        '....#..#',
        '.##.#.##',
        '....#...']

Dijkstra


BFS with a heap: weighted graphs, non-negative weights. Skip stale heap entries.




def dijkstra(g, src):
    dist = defaultdict(lambda: inf)
    dist[src] = 0
    h = [(0, src)]
    while h:
        d, u = heappop(h)
        if d > dist[u]:
            continue                         # stale entry
        for v, w in g[u]:
            if d + w < dist[v]:
                dist[v] = d + w
                heappush(h, (dist[v], v))
    return dict(dist)

Topological sort


Kahn’s algorithm: repeatedly take nodes with in-degree 0. If you can’t take all of them, there is a cycle.




def topo_order(n, prereqs):                  # prereqs: (course, needs)
    g, indeg = defaultdict(list), [0] * n
    for c, p in prereqs:
        g[p].append(c); indeg[c] += 1
    q = deque(i for i in range(n) if indeg[i] == 0)
    order = []
    while q:
        u = q.popleft()
        order.append(u)
        for v in g[u]:
            indeg[v] -= 1
            if indeg[v] == 0:
                q.append(v)
    return order if len(order) == n else []   # [] means a cycle

print(topo_order(4, [(1, 0), (2, 0), (3, 1), (3, 2)]), topo_order(2, [(0, 1), (1, 0)]))

Union-Find


Merge groups and ask “same group?” in near O(1). Path compression + union by size.




class DSU:
    def __init__(self, n):
        self.p, self.size, self.groups = list(range(n)), [1] * n, n
    def find(self, x):
        while self.p[x] != x:
            self.p[x] = self.p[self.p[x]]       # path halving
            x = self.p[x]
        return x
    def union(self, a, b):
        a, b = self.find(a), self.find(b)
        if a == b:
            return False
        if self.size[a] < self.size[b]:
            a, b = b, a
        self.p[b] = a
        self.size[a] += self.size[b]
        self.groups -= 1
        return True

World 13 · Dynamic Programming




1D DP & rolling variables


State = index. If dp[i] only needs the last 1–2 values, keep variables instead of an array.




def climb(n):                          # ways to climb n stairs with 1 or 2 steps
    a, b = 1, 1
    for _ in range(n - 1):
        a, b = b, a + b
    return b

def rob(nums):                         # house robber: no two adjacent
    take, skip = 0, 0
    for x in nums:
        take, skip = skip + x, max(take, skip)
    return max(take, skip)

Kadane: max subarray




def max_subarray(nums):
    best = cur = nums[0]
    for x in nums[1:]:
        cur = max(x, cur + x)          # extend, or restart here
        best = max(best, cur)
    return best

Coin change (unbounded knapsack)


dp[a] = fewest coins to make a. Start with inf, dp[0] = 0.




def coin_change(coins, amount):
    dp = [0] + [inf] * amount
    for a in range(1, amount + 1):
        for c in coins:
            if c <= a:
                dp[a] = min(dp[a], dp[a - c] + 1)
    return dp[amount] if dp[amount] != inf else -1

Top-down with @cache


Write the recurrence, add @cache, done. Great for grids and strings.




@cache
def unique_paths(r, c):
    if r == 0 or c == 0:
        return 1
    return unique_paths(r - 1, c) + unique_paths(r, c - 1)

@cache
def word_break(s, words=('leet', 'code', 'le', 'et')):
    return not s or any(s.startswith(w) and word_break(s[len(w):]) for w in words)

LIS in O(n log n)


tails[k] = smallest tail of any increasing subsequence of length k+1. bisect_left finds where x fits.




def lis(nums):
    tails = []
    for x in nums:
        i = bisect_left(tails, x)
        if i == len(tails):
            tails.append(x)
        else:
            tails[i] = x
    return len(tails)

2D DP: LCS


dp[i][j] uses the first i chars of a and first j of b. Match: diagonal + 1. Otherwise best of up/left.




def lcs(a, b):
    m, n = len(a), len(b)
    dp = [[0] * (n + 1) for _ in range(m + 1)]
    for i in range(1, m + 1):
        for j in range(1, n + 1):
            if a[i - 1] == b[j - 1]:
                dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1
            else:
                dp[i][j] = max(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1])
    return dp[m][n]

        out.append(f'<text class="lbl" x="{10 + (j + 2.5) * cell}" y="{10 + cell / 2}">{_esc(ch)}</text>')
    for i, ch in enumerate(a):
        out.append(f'<text class="lbl" x="{10 + cell / 2}" y="{10 + (i + 2.5) * cell}">{_esc(ch)}</text>')
    for i in range(m + 1):
        for j in range(n + 1):
            x, y = 10 + (j + 1) * cell, 10 + (i + 1) * cell
            known = i == 0 or j == 0 or (i, j) < done_upto or (i, j) == cur
            cls = 'o th' if (i, j) == cur else 'g' if (i, j) in path else 'a' if (i, j) in deps else ''
            out.append(f'<rect class="b {cls}{"" if known else " dim"}" x="{x + 1}" y="{y + 1}" width="{cell - 2}" height="{cell - 2}" rx="4"/>')
            if known:
                out.append(f'<text x="{x + cell / 2}" y="{y + cell / 2}">{dp[i][j]}</text>')
    out.append('</svg>')
    return ''.join(out)

def viz_lcs(fn, a, b):
    def draw(L, txt, ln):
        dp, i, j = L['dp'], L.get('i'), L.get('j')
        if 'return' in txt:
            m, n, path, chars = len(a), len(b), set(), []
            while m and n:
                if a[m - 1] == b[n - 1]:
                    path.add((m, n)); chars.append(a[m - 1]); m, n = m - 1, n - 1
                elif dp[m - 1][n] >= dp[m][n - 1]:
                    m -= 1
                else:
                    n -= 1
            return (dp_svg(a, b, dp, path=path, done_upto=(len(a) + 1, 0)),
                    f'LCS length = <b>{dp[len(a)][len(b)]}</b>, one LCS is <b>{"".join(reversed(chars))}</b> (green path, traced back from the corner)', '')
        if '+ 1' in txt:
            deps = {(i - 1, j - 1)}
            note = f'a[{i - 1}] = {a[i - 1]} equals b[{j - 1}] = {b[j - 1]}: take the <b>diagonal + 1</b> = {dp[i][j]}'
        else:
            deps = {(i - 1, j), (i, j - 1)}
            note = f'{a[i - 1]} ≠ {b[j - 1]}: take the <b>max</b> of up ({dp[i - 1][j]}) and left ({dp[i][j - 1]}) = {dp[i][j]}'
        return dp_svg(a, b, dp, cur=(i, j), deps=deps, done_upto=(i, j)), note, f'i={i} j={j}'

    blank = [[0] * (len(b) + 1) for _ in range(len(a) + 1)]
    frames, _ = make_frames(fn, (a, b), ['dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1', 'dp[i][j] = max(', 'return dp[m][n]'], draw,
                            (dp_svg(a, b, blank, done_upto=(1, 1)), 'Row i, column j answers: LCS of a[:i] and b[:j].', ''))
    stepper({'lcs': {'frames': frames, 'code': code_of(fn)}}, xp_id='viz:lcs')

World 14 · Patterns




Sliding window


Variable window: expand r every step, move l only when the window breaks the rule. O(n).




def longest_unique(s):
    seen = {}                          # char -> last index
    l = best = 0
    for r, c in enumerate(s):
        if c in seen and seen[c] >= l:
            l = seen[c] + 1
        seen[c] = r
        best = max(best, r - l + 1)
    return best

print(longest_unique('abcabcbb'), longest_unique('pwwkew'))
a, k = [2, 1, 5, 1, 3, 2], 3          # fixed window: max sum of k consecutive
cur = sum(a[:k]); best = cur
for i in range(k, len(a)):
    cur += a[i] - a[i - k]
    best = max(best, cur)
print(best)

def viz_window(fn, s):
    def draw(L, txt, ln):
        l, r, c, best = L.get('l', 0), L.get('r'), L.get('c'), L.get('best', 0)
        col = {k: 'a' for k in range(l, r + 1)}
        col[r] = 'o'
        if txt.startswith('l = seen'):
            note = f"'{c}' already sits inside the window → shrink from the left: <b>l = {l}</b>"
        elif txt.startswith('seen[c]'):
            note = f"remember the last index of '{c}': seen['{c}'] = {r}"
        elif txt.startswith('best'):
            win = s[l:r + 1]
            col = {k: 'g' for k in range(l, r + 1)} if r - l + 1 == best else col
            note = f"window <b>'{win}'</b> has {len(win)} distinct chars → best = <b>{best}</b>"
        else:
            return arr_svg(list(s)), f'answer: <b>{L["best"]}</b>', ''
        return arr_svg(list(s), ptr={'l': l, 'r': r}, col=col), note, fmt_vars(L, ['seen', 'best'])

    frames, _ = make_frames(fn, (s,), ['l = seen[c] + 1', 'seen[c] = r', 'best = max', 'return best'], draw,
                            (arr_svg(list(s)), 'Grow the window to the right; shrink from the left when a character repeats.', ''))
    stepper({'longest_unique': {'frames': frames, 'code': code_of(fn)}}, xp_id='viz:window')

Two pointers


On a sorted array, move the pointer that can still improve the answer.




def two_sum_sorted(a, target):
    l, r = 0, len(a) - 1
    while l < r:
        s = a[l] + a[r]
        if s == target:
            return [l, r]
        if s < target:
            l += 1
        else:
            r -= 1
    return []

def three_sum(nums):
    nums.sort()
    res = []
    for i, x in enumerate(nums):
        if i and x == nums[i - 1]:
            continue                      # skip duplicate anchors
        l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
        while l < r:
            s = x + nums[l] + nums[r]
            if s < 0:
                l += 1
            elif s > 0:
                r -= 1
            else:
                res.append([x, nums[l], nums[r]])
                l += 1
                while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l - 1]:
                    l += 1
    return res

print(two_sum_sorted([1, 3, 4, 6, 9], 10), three_sum([-1, 0, 1, 2, -1, -4]))

print(all(s[i] == s[~i] for i in range(len(s) // 2)))     # ~i == -i-1: palindrome check

Prefix sum + hashmap


“Subarray with sum k”: sum(a[i:j]) == k ⇔ P[j] - P[i] == k. Count earlier prefixes equal to P[j] - k.




def subarray_sum(nums, k):
    count, pre, seen = 0, 0, Counter({0: 1})
    for x in nums:
        pre += x
        count += seen[pre - k]
        seen[pre] += 1
    return count

print(subarray_sum([1, 1, 1], 2), subarray_sum([1, 2, 3, -3, 1], 3))

Sliding window maximum (monotonic deque)


The deque holds indices whose values decrease, so the front is always the window max.




def window_max(a, k):
    dq, out = deque(), []
    for i, x in enumerate(a):
        while dq and a[dq[-1]] <= x:
            dq.pop()
        dq.append(i)
        if dq[0] <= i - k:
            dq.popleft()
        if i >= k - 1:
            out.append(a[dq[0]])
    return out

print(window_max([1, 3, -1, -3, 5, 3, 6, 7], 3))

def _same_groups(got, want):
    norm = lambda g: sorted(sorted(x) for x in g)
    return norm(got) == norm(want)

def _two_sum_ok(got, want):
    nums, target = want
    return (isinstance(got, (list, tuple)) and len(got) == 2 and got[0] != got[1]
            and all(isinstance(i, int) and 0 <= i < len(nums) for i in got) and nums[got[0]] + nums[got[1]] == target)

def _as_set(got, want):
    return len(got) == len(want) and set(got) == set(want)

def _lists(got, want):
    return [list(x) for x in got] == want

def group_anagrams_solution(words):
    groups = defaultdict(list)
    for w in words:
        groups[''.join(sorted(w))].append(w)
    return list(groups.values())

def two_sum_solution(nums, target):
    pos = {}
    for i, x in enumerate(nums):
        if target - x in pos:
            return [pos[target - x], i]
        pos[x] = i

def is_valid_parens_solution(s):
    pair, st = {')': '(', ']': '[', '}': '{'}, []
    for ch in s:
        if ch in pair:
            if not st or st.pop() != pair[ch]:
                return False
        else:
            st.append(ch)
    return not st

💡 hintSort by start. If the next start is <= the last end, extend that end with max; otherwise append a new interval.









🔓 Spoiler: reference solution

def merge_intervals_solution(intervals):
    out = []
    for s, e in sorted(intervals):
        if out and s <= out[-1][1]:
            out[-1][1] = max(out[-1][1], e)
        else:
            out.append([s, e])
    return out

⚔️ Halve It: Search Insert Position  ·  🪙 20
🎯 Quest open. Edit the function above and re-run this cell. 6 hidden tests are waiting.
💡 hintYou want the first index whose value is >= target: that is exactly bisect_left. Or write the lo/hi loop yourself.









🔓 Spoiler: reference solution

def search_insert_solution(nums, target):
    lo, hi = 0, len(nums)
    while lo < hi:
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        if nums[mid] < target:
            lo = mid + 1
        else:
            hi = mid
    return lo

⚔️ Final Boss: Number of Islands  ·  🪙 30
🎯 Quest open. Edit the function above and re-run this cell. 5 hidden tests are waiting.
💡 hintScan every cell. When you find an unvisited "1", count one island and flood-fill (BFS or DFS) to mark all of it visited.









🔓 Spoiler: reference solution

def num_islands_solution(grid):
    if not grid:
        return 0
    R, C = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    seen, count = set(), 0
    for r in range(R):
        for c in range(C):
            if grid[r][c] == '1' and (r, c) not in seen:
                count += 1
                q = deque([(r, c)])
                seen.add((r, c))
                while q:
                    x, y = q.popleft()
                    for dx, dy in ((1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1)):
                        nx, ny = x + dx, y + dy
                        if 0 <= nx < R and 0 <= ny < C and grid[nx][ny] == '1' and (nx, ny) not in seen:
                            seen.add((nx, ny))
                            q.append((nx, ny))
    return count
